hotspot.title: 展覽介紹
hotspot.description:
「Practice and Practice：李錦繡、謝貽娟與我」以兩位嘉義出生女性藝術家李錦繡（1953–2003）與謝貽娟（1967–2017）為核心，透過作品、日常習作、實驗創作與教案，展現她們面對藝術、自我與他人之間的思考與實踐歷程。展覽亦由蔡志賢、康雅筑、王怡婷三位藝術家，透過田調與現地創作，共構跨世代對話，重新看見兩位嘉義當代藝術家的藝術與生命實踐。
1990年代開始，女性藝術逐漸受美術館重視，在經歷不同階段的展覽與歷史整理之後，近年各美術館更進一步關注女性的多重身分與社會角色，而形塑出不同視角和定位的展覽。於此脈絡下，嘉義市立美術館也關切此一議題，透過李錦繡與謝貽娟兩位早逝的女性藝術家，觀察她們如何在有限生命中迸發無限能量，也反思如何突破既有的性別論述框架予以重述及擴展。本展嘗試從李錦繡既有的高度評價之上，揭示她精妙融合書法線條的創作方法，以及投身兒童教育、奉獻自我的一面；從謝貽娟身上，則著重一位藝術家奮力的自我養成，是如何運用大量練習、自畫像、速寫本與複合媒材，建構自我與空間的對話。
展題「Practice and Practice」意為「實踐」和「練習」，透過研究與策劃，展覽不僅止是單純的作品觀看與賞析，也強調藝術創作中的實踐性與過程性，並從藝術家的作品和思想，進一步延伸至觀者之眼，開拓出第三空間。
展覽以三個子題：「我與我們」、「加與減」、「方圓之外」，開展兩位創作者的生命與藝術之關聯，共計展出包含油畫、水彩、壓克力、版畫、攝影、複合媒材等平面創作共100多件，畫家手稿、速寫本、生活物件及檔案照片等相關物件近90件，另外特別呈現三組共同創作，期許觀者可從中認識此對應與連結於時間進程中不斷演變、不斷被重賦意義所呈顯的多重面貌與內涵，深切感受藝術家實踐與練習的精神與能量。

hotspot.title: Exhibition Overview
hotspot.description: Chiayi-born women artists—Lii Jiin Shiow (1953-2003) and Jo Hsieh (1967-2017), the Practice and Practice with LII Jiin Shiow and Jo HSIEH exhibition presents their journeys of thoughts and practices within the realms of art, the self, and others through their works, quotidian studies, experimental creations, and lesson plans. The exhibition also includes three artists—Tsai Chih-hsien, Kang Ya-chu, and Wang Yi-ting, who engage in cross-generational dialogues through field researches and site-specific works, revisiting the artistic and life practices of the two contemporary artists from Chiayi. Since the 1990s, women’s art has been increasingly emphasized by art museums. After undergoing various stages of exhibitions and historical compilations, in recent years, art museums have further focused on the multiple identities and social roles of women, organizing exhibitions from different perspectives and positions. In this context, the Chiayi Art Museum is also concerned about this issue. Through featuring the two women artists, Lii Jiin Shiow and Jo Hsieh, who passed away in their middle age, the museum explores how their boundless energy emerged despite their limited lifespans, and reflects on how to challenge the established framework of gender discourse for reinterpretation and expansion. The exhibition attempts to reveal, based on the existing high regard for Lii, her creative approaches that ingeniously incorporated calligraphic lines, as well as her dedication to children’s education and selfless devotion. For Hsieh, the exhibition highlights her dedicated journey of self-development, showcasing how she built a dialogue between herself and space through extensive practice, self-portraits, sketchbooks, and mixed media. The “Practice and Practice” in the exhibition title refers to both “the act of putting ideas into action” and “the process of repeated practice.” Through research and curating, the exhibition is not merely about viewing and appreciating works, but also emphasizes the practice and process of art-making. Furthermore, from the artists’ works and ideas, it extends to the viewer’s perspective, opening up a third space. Organized into three sub-themes—“I, We, and the In-Between,” “More and Less,” and “Outside the Form,” the exhibition delves into the relationship between the lives and art of the two artists. It showcases over 100 two-dimensional works, including oil paintings, watercolors, acrylic paintings, prints, photographs, and mixed media. It also features nearly 90 related items such as the artists’ manuscripts, sketchbooks, everyday objects, and archival photographs. In addition, three co-creations are specially presented. Viewers will gain insight into the multiple facets and meanings of their contrasts and connections, which constantly evolve and are redefined over time, deeply experiencing the spirit and energy of the artists’ “practice and practice.”

hotspot.title: 李錦繡/ LII Jiin Shiow（1953–2003）
hotspot.description:
嘉義出生，自幼展現藝術天分，畢業於國立臺灣師範大學美術系，1980年代赴法國巴黎高等裝飾藝術學院進修。返臺後她投身創作與教育，並協助家人從事兒童藝術教育。她的創作形式涵蓋繪畫、書法與裝置等，且善用日常物件為媒材，作品結合東方書道與西方構成，呈現自由靈動的藝術語彙。1990年代她活躍於臺灣前衛藝術圈，其開創性極具指標性。因個性低調且多工繁忙，她生前並不積極籌辦個展，身後作品則陸續有大型展出及相關研究。
Born in Chiayi, Lii Jiin Shiow displayed a talent for art from an early age. She graduated from the Department of Fine Arts at National Taiwan Normal University, and, in the 1980s, she went to Paris, France for further studies and enrolled in the École Nationale Supérieure des Arts Décoratifs. After returning to Taiwan, she engaged in creative practice and teaching, and assisted her family in children’s art education. Working in painting, calligraphy, installation, and other forms, Lii was skilled at using everyday objects as creative media. Her work integrates Eastern calligraphy and Western composition, demonstrating a free-spirited and dynamic artistic vocabulary. She was active in Taiwan's avant-garde art scene in the 1990s, with her pioneering works being highly iconic. Due to her low profile and busy schedule, she was not active in organizing solo exhibitions during her lifetime. However, after her passing, her works have been continuously exhibited on a large scale, accompanied by ongoing research.

hotspot.title: 作品簡介/ Artwork Introduction
hotspot.description:
自畫像/ Self Portrait
李錦繡喜歡「灰」，熱衷於表現灰色調帶來的模糊狀態，甚至是一種之於表象之「光」的另一面「影」。本件《自畫像》表現所處環境的黑暗，前端透進幾絲光線，人物的臉龐到手臂之間反射灰綠色的光影，後方牆壁也有光影呈現的色域。李錦繡於抽象與具象之間、內與外之間，將自我的情緒和詭譎的氛圍表現得曖昧不清，綠、紫與橘的幾抹顏色，也成了灰色裡的點綴和靈氣。
Fond of the color gray, Lii Jiin Shiow was keen on expressing the ambiguity conveyed by gray tones, or even shadow as the counterpart to the light of appearances. The work Self Portrait depicts a dim environment with a few rays of light coming through the front. From the face to the arms, the subject reflects a play of gray-green light and shadow. The wall in the background also displays a range of tones shaped by light and shadow. Navigating between the abstract and the figurative, the interior and the exterior, Lii expresses her emotions and an eerie atmosphere in an ambiguous way. Colors of green, purple, and orange punctuate the gray tones, exuding a sense of etherealness.

hotspot.title: 謝貽娟/ Jo Hsieh（1967–2017）
hotspot.description:
嘉義出生，自青少年時期即對藝術展現強烈意志，國中畢業後就讀復興商工，1990年代赴英國進修，1998年取得英國皇家藝術學院碩士，2002年取得費爾茅斯藝術學院藝術哲學博士學位。她長期旅居英國，發展出以「非空間」（None-Space）為核心概念的創作系列，善用藍色、幾何與複合媒材表現內在狀態。2015年她回到臺灣仍持續創作，生前多次參與在英國、美國與臺灣等地的展覽，身後由家人成立基金會持續推廣其藝術。
Born in Chiayi, Jo Hsieh showed a strong aspiration for art from her teenage years, and she entered the Fu-Hsin Trade & Arts School after graduating from the junior high school. In the 1990s, she pursued advanced studies in the UK, earning a master’s degree from the Royal College of Art in 1998 and a doctoral degree in Philosophy of Art from Falmouth College of Art in 2002. During her long residence in the UK, Hsieh developed a series of works centered around the concept of “None-Space,” employing blue tones, geometric elements, and mixed media to express her inner state. In 2015, she returned to Taiwan and continued her creative practice. Throughout her lifetime, she participated in numerous exhibitions in the UK, the USA, and Taiwan; after her passing, her family established a foundation to continuously promote her art.

hotspot.title: 作品簡介/ Artwork Introduction
hotspot.description:
Dreamland III
謝貽娟短短五十年的一生，卻畫有1600餘張的自畫像，從1993年起，她每日都在英國住處的角落畫自畫像，間或持續至1999年。這張版畫算是自畫像的第一張，由四個方塊組成的構圖中，中間為謝貽娟人像，周圍以線條表現頭髮、物象和自然，再以灰黑和黃之對比，呈現多樣的面貌以及標題中的「夢境」。
During her short life of 50 years, Jo Hsieh produced over 1,600 self-portraits. From 1993 to 1999, she created one almost every day in a corner of her residence in the UK. Considered the first of these self-portraits, this print is composed of four rectangular sections, with Hsieh’s image at the center surrounded by linear depictions of hair, objects, and nature. The contrast between gray-black and yellow presents varied visual elements and suggests the “dreamland” of the title.

hotspot.title: 我與我們/ I, We, and the In-Between
hotspot.description:
以藝術家的自畫像與人像創作為出發，呈現她們從個體意識到群體關係的探索。李錦繡自1970年代即關注人與自我的關係，從同儕、家庭到社會，透過灰色調與光影，捕捉倒影與逆光中的自我形象。她以線條留存輪廓與過程，發展出帶有攝影語言與負片效果的人像系列，展現「我與群」之間的曖昧與交錯。
謝貽娟則以「自畫像」作為日記，記錄自身與環境、物件、動物之間的互動與感知。離鄉到英國，她在異地持續尋找「根」，將童年經驗、家鄉記憶融入畫作。「人」形圖騰在她作品中跳躍，展現她對自我與他者的反覆凝視與解析。
從她們的創作可見「我」如何在變動中被重新定義，也見證她們如何藉藝術實踐與生活對話，追尋內在的安放與自處。從具象到抽象，從線條到色彩，兩位藝術家在不同途徑中，找到自我的定位。
I, We, and the In-Between Focusing on the artists’ self-portraits and portraits, this section presents their exploration from individual consciousness to collective relationships. Since the 1970s, Lii Jiin Shiow had developed a keen interest in the relationship between people and the self, including peers, family, and society. Through gray tones and the interplay of light and shadow, she captured her self-image from reflections and backlighting. Using lines to preserve contours and processes, she created a series of portraits integrating photographic language and the effects of negative imagery, which represented the ambiguity and interlacing between “I and the group.” Like keeping a diary, Jo Hsieh painted self-portraits to record her interactions with and perceptions of the environment, objects, and animals. After leaving her hometown for the UK, she continued to search for her “roots” abroad and infused her childhood experiences and memories of her hometown into her paintings. The totems of “human form” leap across her works, manifesting her repeated gaze and analysis of the self and the other. From the two artists’ works, we can observe how the concept of “I” is redefined in a constantly changing context, and witness how they, through artistic practice, engaged in a dialogue with life and sought inner peace and self-settlement. From the figurative to the abstract, from lines to colors, they found their own sense of identity through different paths.

hotspot.title: 作品簡介/ Artwork Introduction
hotspot.description:
婚禮/ The Wedding
這件作品創作於李錦繡探索自我的時期，當時的她經常以群像為主軸，繪寫家族、婚姻與密不可分的親情。李錦繡曾在論文中提及自己喜愛灰色，因為其模糊性及曖昧性。這件作品以灰黑、模糊的形式呈現家族婚禮合照場景，一改清晰的模樣，借用攝影負片的效果，反轉明暗與黑白的關係，在灰色與黑色的主調中留下人形和輪廓。
This work was created during the period when Lii Jiin Shiow focused on the exploration of the self, often using group portraits to depict family, marriage, and the deep bonds of kinship. Lii once expressed in her essay her fondness for the color gray because of its obscurity and ambiguity. Subverting photographic clarity, this work features a blurred, gray-black toned family wedding portrait. It draws on the effects of negative imagery to reverse the relationship between light and dark, black and white, leaving silhouetted figures in a gray-black palette.

作品簡介/ Artwork Introduction
hotspot.description:
對影/ A Pair of Shadows
1970年代中期，李錦繡展開長達七年的家族照片系列創作。這系列靈感來自攝影底片的負片效果，經常以灰、黑色為基調，主題為個人生命、日常生活，描繪對象為家人手足、同學朋友。最初畫面經常有黑色團塊圍繞在人物周邊，形成畫面空間的層次。本作《對影》以弟弟李英哲為對象，畫面中兩個人物以相同的坐姿前後並列，神貌模糊，具有相似又相異的趣味。
In the mid-1970s, Lii Jiin Shiow began a seven-year series of works based on family photographs. Inspired by the effects of negative imagery, this series often features gray and black as its dominant tones and explores themes of personal life and everyday experience, depicting family members, siblings, classmates, and friends. In the early pieces of this series, black masses frequently surround the figures to create a layered pictorial space. This work, A Pair on Shadows, portrays the artist’s younger brother, Lii Ying-che. With their faces rendered ambiguously, the two figures sit one behind the other in identical postures, showing interesting resemblances and differences.

hotspot.title: 作品簡介/ Artwork Introduction
hotspot.description:
無題/ Untitled
《無題》以油彩繪製而成，畫中遠景是美麗的山群，前景是一群共舞的人們。這幅畫靈感來自謝貽娟母親過去所任教的嘉義竹崎一帶的風景，源於她自童年到成長期的經驗。本作也是她尚未轉入抽象之前、較爲早期也較為具象的風景作品，畫中可見嘉義的自然、山脈，以及人文風情，也是她與嘉義的深刻連結。對謝貽娟來說，嘉義是「適合歸返、療癒、作畫和找尋自我的地方」。
The oil painting Untitled delineates a beautiful mountain range in the background and a group of dancing figures in the foreground. This painting draws inspiration from the landscapes of Jhuci in Chiayi, where Jo Hsieh’s mother once taught, as well as from her childhood and formative experiences. Created before her transition into abstraction, this is one of Hsieh’s earlier and more figurative landscape paintings. The natural scenery, mountain forms, and cultural imagery illustrated in the work reflect her deep connection to Chiayi. For Hsieh, Chiayi is “a place for returning, healing, painting, and self-discovery.”

hotspot.title: 作品簡介/ Artwork Introduction
hotspot.description:
自我的探尋/ The Search of Self
本作的構圖彷如一種電影「分鏡」般的結構，也像是動畫中的逐格敘事。是李錦繡在巴黎時期經常實驗的空間型態，有時讓空間反射多重倒影，有時描繪連續時間中不斷改變的影像與空間。此作可見日後《任遨遊》系列的空間分割與探索，其中潛藏著自己與所在環境物件的物我、人我關係，以及與空間關係所進行的對話。
The composition of this work resembles a film storyboard or a frame-by-frame narrative in animation. It reflects the kind of spatial structure that Lii Jiin Shiow often experimented with during her time in Paris, sometimes incorporating multiple mirrored reflections, and sometimes depicting shifting images and spaces across continuous time. This work foreshadows the spatial segmentation and exploration found in her later Roaming Everywhere series, revealing subtle dialogues between the self and the surrounding objects, between the self and others, and between the self and the space.

hotspot.title: 作品簡介/ Artwork Introduction
hotspot.description:
時空記憶（獨）/ Memory of Space and Time (alone)
李錦繡曾說：「透明的空間，我的存在應也是透明自在。」1990年代之後，家中的室內空間成為李錦繡主要的作畫題材，從早期自畫像到後期家居空間，可以看見畫家從人物、自我的變化，移情至物件和空間。李錦繡一生大部分時間都奉獻給家人，她在家中有限的空間中作畫，灰色調成為模糊和沒有界線的延伸，顯得透明自在。畫中一張色彩明亮的「椅子」，成為她寄情自我的載體，最終也是一種自我存在的遨遊與自由，造就屬於自己的另一種「自畫像」。
Lii Jiin Shiow once said: “In a transparent space, my existence should also be transparent and free.” From the 1990s onward, the interior space of her home became the main theme of her work. From early self-portraits to later depictions of domestic interiors, the artist gradually shifted her focus from figures and personal changes to objects and space. With most of her life dedicated to her family, Lii painted within the confined space of her home. The gray tones in her work evoke a sense of obscurity and boundlessness, conveying feelings of transparency and ease. In this painting, a brightly colored “chair” becomes a symbol of self-expression, which ultimately represents a free and roaming existence, and forms an alternative “self-portrait.”

hotspot.title: 作品簡介/ Artwork Introduction
hotspot.description:
無題/ Untitled
謝貽娟說：「藍色是沈靜的，不張狂的，一種理性的姿態，一種精神上的穩定，一種心靈上的平衡。」在探索自然與物理世界的表象、內容之間，她最終用單色、幾何的方式，呈現自身收穫與感知，在一片藍色礦物粉末中，濃縮世界觀與精神性的參透。創作中的勞動也是謝貽娟找尋自我與體悟的過程，她說「沒有人懂我在說什麼，只有畫畫懂我」，畫是她自己，一片藍色和純粹的幾何，是她自處與延伸的宇宙，也是她所凝鍊的「自畫像」。
Jo Hsieh said: “The color blue, calm and unassuming, is a rational stance, a mental steadiness, and a spiritual balance.” While exploring the representations and essences of the natural and physical world, she ultimately turned to monochromic and geometric forms to express her own insights and perceptions. Within the blue mineral powder, she distilled a worldview and spiritual clarity. In Hsieh’s work, the labor of creative practice is also the process of discovering and understanding the self. She said: “No one understands what I am saying, except painting.” Painting represents herself, while the blue tones and pure geometry form a universe where she both dwelt and expanded, as well as the “self-portraits” she carefully crafted.

hotspot.description: 無憂無慮 Free of Worries 蓄意的 With Purpose 2025 鐵雕和風有關，過度用力會傷了時間；凝視材料， 拆解與再造，羞澀且沉重的雙腿，浮上了聲響。 這組作品來自彼此，命中有命；鐵雕與愛有關，絮語與叨唸，很難分得清，看著《無憂無慮》線之流動，自動長出了肉感的心臟。 My metal sculptures are connected to the wind; too much force can wound time. The metal sculptures are intertwined with love, with whispers and mutterings that are hardly distinguishable. As your eyes follow the flowing lines of Free of Worries, a fleshy heart quietly appears.

His works are primarily abstract or semi-abstract, characterized by a profound and understated aesthetic.

hotspot.title: 加與減/ More and Less
hotspot.description:
在創作中，藝術家總在嘗試之間進行加與減。李錦繡跳脫學院訓練，於創作中借用書法筆勢、展現線條動態，也運用日常物件，在畫面中融入光影、留白與挖空等方式，實驗空間與形體的關係。同時李錦繡也致力藝術教育，將日常融入藝術，她在幼兒園的現地製作與個人創作，亦擅長以金屬、磚瓦、衣物等為媒材，轉化日常為造境，展現物我之間的流動與共感。
謝貽娟善用粉末、纖維與版畫等媒材，以線條與幾何組構畫面，將水、天、藍化為形式語彙。她的創作展現反覆、緩慢與細膩的勞動感，尤能以來回的線條、重複的形狀、牽引的色塊，組織豐富的音樂與律動性。此外，速寫本與草圖則記錄著日復一日的實驗過程與思考痕跡，亦為面對自我的持續練習。
本區納入蔡志賢與王怡婷的回應創作，分別以雕塑與自然材質介入，延伸兩位藝術家的創作思路，讓觀者不僅看到作品，更能體驗藝術家的實踐精神。
In the creative process, artists are always experimenting with adding more or less. Lii Jiin Shiow broke away from academic training and drew on calligraphy strokes to express dynamic lines in her works. She also incorporated everyday objects into her paintings, using light and shadow, negative space, and hollowing out to experiment with the relationship between space and form. In addition to her creative practice, Lii was dedicated to art education, integrating everyday life into her art. In her site-specific works for the kindergarten and her personal creations, she masterfully employed materials such as metal, bricks, tiles, and clothes to transform everyday life into a constructed environment, through which she illustrated the flow and empathy between objects and herself. Jo Hsieh skillfully used powders, fibers, prints, and other media, composing her works with lines and geometric elements to transform water, sky, and blue into a vocabulary of forms. Her works exude a repeated, slow, and delicate sense of labor. She was particularly adept at using back-and-forth lines, repeated shapes, and interplaying color patches to create rich musicality and rhythm. Moreover, her sketchbooks and drafts, which document the day-to-day processes of experimentation and traces of thought, reveal a continuous practice of self-reflection. This section also features Tsai Chih-hsien and Wang Yi-ting, who respond to the exhibition using sculptures and natural materials, respectively. Their works extend the creative concepts of Lii and Hsieh, inviting viewers not only to appreciate their works but also to experience their spirit of practice.

hotspot.description:
通靈/ Psychic
李錦繡於留法前後，即已積極在紙上探索空間、具象及抽象的關係，有時是有生命體及無生命體之結合，有時是尺度之於空間的、幾何的變形。 從她的速寫本之中，可以看到她從人像到物象之間的捕捉與探索，若再對照《通靈》一作，畫中的椅子是焦點，藍色區域中的線條，延伸至後景中看似人像的團塊，既抽象又具象，也開啟了李錦繡日後表現畫面分割、以物寄情和象徵自處的方式。
Around the time she left for France, Lii Jiin Shiow was already actively exploring the relationship among space, figuration, and abstraction on paper, sometimes combining animate and inanimate forms, and sometimes engaging with spatial scale and geometric transformation. Her sketchbooks reveal her captures and explorations ranging from human figures to object imagery. In comparison, this painting, Psychic, focuses on a chair with lines within the blue area extending toward a human-like mass in the background. Both abstract and figurative, the work anticipates Lii’s later approach to pictorial segmentation, emotional expression through objects, and symbolic reflections on selfhood.

hotspot.description:
謝貽娟擅長以畫筆展現不同媒材和材料的質地。本件《無題》以畫筆呈現出纖維般的的質感，繽紛的色塊呈現拼布的樣態，錯落的顏色也表現出她作品中常見的音樂性，也造就出童趣。本作可搭配她筆記本一起觀看，尤其是其中的色彩和圖騰表現。
Jo Hsieh was skilled at using the brush to express the textures of various materials. In Untitled, brushstrokes render a fibrous surface, while vibrant blocks of color resemble a patchwork composition. The interplay of hues reflects the musicality often seen in her works and conveys a sense of childlike fun. This work may be viewed alongside her notebooks, particularly in relation to her use of color and totemic forms.

hotspot.description:
謝貽娟一直以來都展現出對於水、天空、大自然的興趣，也用各種形式表現天空和水的型態、自然與自我的關係，她的作品中也經常以「手」搭配物件和環境。本件照相腐蝕版畫《Space Form III》，表現了一隻手的探觸，以「手」的介入影射創作的過程，手也彷彿代表謝貽娟的自我，在水波及光暈中有如同心圓一般散開，於有限空間延伸，展現自我的渺小存在以及與自然的無窮盡之對話。
Consistently drawn to themes of water, sky, and nature, Jo Hsieh presented the forms of sky and water through various means, reflecting on the relationship between nature and the self. In her works, the image of the hand frequently appears alongside objects and environmental elements. In the photo etching Space Form III, a hand is shown reaching outward. This gesture of intervention suggests the creative process, with the hand serving as a symbol of the artist herself. Amid ripples and halos that spread like concentric circles, the hand extends within a confined space, evoking the smallness of the self and its endless dialogue with nature.

Her work often employs space to compose rhythmic relationships among time, space, material, image, and energy, constructing fluid spiritual landscapes shaped by poetic language and acute perception.

hotspot.title: 作品資訊/ Artwork Information
hotspot.description: 呼吸 Breathing 2025 本裝置作品以「繪畫線條」為核心，運用臺灣桂竹與黃銅線構成懸浮於空間中的不規則圓形結構。線條如同未完成的手稿樂譜，交錯牽引，映照著觀者與作品間無形的節奏與氣流。 素材使用了李錦繡所留下的教材紙張及黃銅片，紙張代表記憶殘片，黃銅則賦予視覺律動感。結構設計呼應謝貽娟手稿中的音樂性線條，透過纖維質感與金屬光澤，創造出視覺與材質雙重律動的「無聲音樂」。整體呈現持續呼吸的空間書寫，邀請觀者透過凝視與移動，感知視覺與身體之間的微妙共鳴。 Centering on the idea of “drawn lines,” this installation features a floating, irregular circular structure made of Makino bamboo and brass wire. The lines, intertwining and pulling against one another, resemble an unfinished musical manuscript, echoing the invisible rhythms and airflows between the viewer and the work. This work incorporates paper and brass pieces from the lesson materials left by Lii Jiin Shiow. The paper serves as fragments of memory, while the brass gives a sense of visual rhythm. The structural design echoes the musical lines found in Jo Hsieh’s manuscripts, using the fibrous texture and the metal luster to create a “silent music” shaped by both visual and material rhythms. Altogether, the work represents a spatial composition in constant breath, inviting viewers to sense a subtle resonance between vision and the body through gaze and motion.

hotspot.title: 方圓之外/ Outside the Form
hotspot.description:
探索兩位藝術家對空間的哲學思維與感知路徑。李錦繡關心人類占據的「空間」神祕性，作品中常於灰色調和均勻色調中點綴色彩，構成「移動」的意象，畫面有如小行星般游移與對話，展現自由與探索的動力。
謝貽娟則從日常物件與環境出發，追求「非空間」的表現。她以藍色與幾何為主調，營造簡潔卻蘊含豐富情感的畫面，對空間與人我關係進行抽象詮釋，創造出靜謐而深層的心靈場域。
本展區由蔡志賢以雕塑延伸李錦繡與謝貽娟的線條與動勢，康雅筑則以纖維織品回應兩位藝術家的實踐精神與與嘉義的土地連結，共同描繪她們對自由、空間與生命的實踐和追尋。觀者可在畫面與形式之外，感知藝術家如何追尋內在與外部的宇宙及其超越。
This section examines the philosophical thoughts and perceptual trajectories of the two artists regarding space. Lii Jiin Shiow was fascinated by the mystery of the “space” inhabited by humans. In her works, the gray hues and uniform tones accented with colors create images of “movement,” which resemble the scenes of roaming and interacting asteroids, embodying the dynamics of freedom and exploration. Starting from everyday objects and environments, Jo Hsieh pursued the expression of “None-Space.” With a focus on blue tones and geometry, she created simple yet emotionally rich images, offering an abstract interpretation of the relationship among space, the self, and others, and constructing a tranquil and profound spiritual realm. The section also showcases sculptures by Tsai Chih-hsien, which extend the lines and dynamic gestures of Lii and Hsieh, alongside a fiber textile by Kang Ya-chu, which responds to their spirit of practice and their connection to the land of Chiayi. Both Tsai and Kang reflect the practice and pursuit of freedom, space, and life by the two women artists. Beyond the images and forms, viewers can perceive how the artists seek and even transcend both their inner world and the external universe.

hotspot.title: 作品介紹/ Artwork Introduction
hotspot.description:
對話/ Conversation
本作為李錦繡於1990年代後常見之居家空間主題之作，深刻表現了空間中的多樣物件與多重視點，畫中灰色調的場域回應了李錦繡對「存在」的體察，在「模糊」與「灰色」之間，物件凌亂卻又有各自的位置，涵蓋了交流與凝視。
作品具有第一人稱到第三人稱的感知方式，也是李錦繡一貫創作的特質。畫外擺放的兩把椅子，以「第三人稱」的方式觀照著繪畫，像是一個旁觀者和局外人；而兩把椅子同時也表徵李錦繡的自我，椅子是讓人乘坐的物件，也是人以「第一人稱」參與其所處環境的定位和視點；最後，《對話〉這件作品的名稱以第二人稱定名，在面對之間，話語、視線交流，讓我和物的存在，於空間中有更多遐想。
Focusing on domestic interiors, a recurring theme in Lii Jiin Shiow’s work since the 1990s, this piece delineates a rich array of objects within the space from multiple perspectives. The gray-toned setting reflects Lii’s contemplation of existence. Within the obscurity and grayness, the seemingly scattered objects are nonetheless purposefully placed, implying a sense of interaction and mutual gaze.
The work shifts between first-person and third-person perspectives, a consistent characteristic of Lii’s artistic approach. The two chairs positioned outside the painting are like bystanders or outsiders, engaging with the painting from a third-person point of view. At the same time, they symbolize the artist herself, not only as functional objects for sitting, but also as markers of a first-person presence within the environment. Finally, the title of this work, Conversation, invokes a second-person engagement. Through this encounter, words and gazes are exchanged, allowing room for reflection on the existence of both the self and the object.

Skillfully working with found objects, he gives them new life through welding, assemblage, and reconstruction. His works are primarily abstract or semi-abstract, characterized by a profound and understated aesthetic.

hotspot.title: 作品介紹/ Artwork Introduction
hotspot.description: 傍晚別離 Evening Farewell 等什麼呢 Waiting for What 還是忘記 Still Forgetting 2025 鐵雕和風有關，過度用力會傷了時間；凝視材料， 拆解與再造，羞澀且沉重的雙腿，浮上了聲響。 創作和意志有關，《傍晚別離》、《等什麼呢》、《還是忘記》，全是帶著語氣的一生懸命。 My metal sculptures are connected to the wind; too much force can wound time. I gaze into the materials, dismantling and reconstructing them. Shy and heavy legs resonate with sound. Creative practice is driven by willpower. Evening Farewell, Waiting for What, and Still Forgetting all carry a distinct emotional tone, each created with all-out devotion.

hotspot.title: 作品介紹/ Artwork Introduction
hotspot.description:
無題/ Untitled
本作在一層上了底色的紙張上，嘗試以油彩畫上彎繞的線條，再繪製直向的線條，並陸續加入不同顏色的曲線，由細轉粗，增加力道與速度。漸漸地，油畫顏料和紙的纖維產生突起和肌理，每條線也出現毛邊與裂縫。謝貽娟在連續的轉動與來回之間，在動態的身體與重複的形式中，結構出平面之中多層次的韻律感。
On a sheet of primed paper, this work experiments with curved lines drawn in oil paint, adding straight lines and gradually incorporating thin to thick curves of different colors to intensify force and speed. Progressively, the oil paint and paper fibers produce raised textures, with each line developing frayed edges and cracks. Through continuously rotating and back-and-forth brushstrokes, Jo Hsieh employs a dynamic gesture and repetitive forms to compose a multilayered sense of rhythm on a flat surface.

hotspot.description:
無題/ Untitled
「手」作為謝貽娟創作時重要工具，她時常徒手於畫面上推開礦物粉末，進入無邊的深沉的藍色之中，再以具有穿透力的的金銀礦物粉末，堆積出畫面中的肌理和層次，創造出光影的變化。媒材與媒材之間的接觸和疊合，也像是空間與空間的交疊，透過不同的光線和角度觀察，會有不同的感受。
The hand was a vital tool in Jo Hsieh’s creative process. She often spread mineral powder across the surface with her bare hands, immersing herself in the boundless depth of blue. With the addition of penetrating gold and silver powders, she built up textures and layers that produce shifting effects of light and shadow. In the resulting works, the contact and overlap between materials evoke the interweaving of spaces, offering varied sensory experiences when viewed from different angles and under changing light.

hotspot.title: 作品介紹/ Artwork Introduction
hotspot.description:
牽扯/ Involvement
李錦繡拜師嘉義書法家陳丁奇鑽研書道，將書法的線性、飛白等融入於繪畫創作的線條，寫字的韌勁用於作畫上，成為樹木恣意生長的生命力。《牽扯》同樣展現著李錦繡偏愛的灰色調，加上白色以及充滿生命韌性的黑色線條，表現樹木生長的枝幹以及蜷曲向上的力量。
Lii Jiin Shiow studied calligraphy under the Chiayi-based calligrapher Chen Ding-chi. She incorporated calligraphic elements such as lines and hollow strokes into the lines of her paintings, and applied the force of calligraphic brushwork to render her works, creating the vitality of freely growing trees. The work Involvement showcases Lii’s signature gray palette, enhanced with white and dynamic black lines that embody strength and life, symbolizing the growing branches and their upward, spiraling force.

hotspot.title: 作品介紹/ Artwork Introduction
hotspot.description: 線延伸出的那些漪 As Lines Are Drawn, Ripples Begin 2025 在李錦繡與謝貽娟的創作過程中那些素描練習與對於線條的思考，總是不斷地提問、練習與創造，她們的思路是交錯媒材、是纏繞故事、是鉤織時光、亦是紡捻生命。我在李錦繡留下的材料中找到了一根木製線軸，是纖維紡捻成紗線製成線筒時的支軸，它記錄著時代與產業的更迭。 我彷如看到了藝術家創作的核心，作品圍繞著藝術家的生命歷程而紡捻淬煉。因此透過線條與色彩呈現兩位藝術家的生命力，一根根管狀彩色編織垂懸而下，與地上的藍色織毯相互對話，藉此感受藝術家在作品中留下的能量、敘事與痕跡。似樹、似根、似水、似浪，致敬她們奉獻給創作的生命。 In the creative process of Lii Jiin Shiow and Jo Hsieh, their drawing studies and reflections on lines were acts of constant questioning, practicing, and making. Their ways of thinking intertwined media, entangled stories, wove time, and spun life. Among the materials Lii left behind, I discovered a wooden spool, which was once the core shaft used in spinning fibers into yarn for bobbin-making. It records the shifts of time and industry. I feel as if I have seen the cores of the artists’ creative spirits, and my work is spun and refined around the threads of their life journeys. Through the renderings of lines and colors, their vitality is made visible. Tubular, colorful weavings hang down and enter into dialogue with the blue tapestry on the ground, evoking the energy, narrative, and traces the artists have left within their works. Like trees, roots, water, and waves, this work is a tribute to the lives they devoted to art-making.

hotspot.title: 藝術家介紹/ Artist Introduction
hotspot.description: 康雅筑（1980-） KANG Ya-chu 擅長運用纖維編織、自然材質等複合媒材，探討工藝技能與體力勞動、生活狀態與遷徙移動、經濟貿易與社會結構之間的關係，主題經常探討身份、人與自然關係，以及社會環境等議題。 Kang Ya-chu works with mixed media, including woven fibers and natural materials, to explore the relationships between craftsmanship and physical labor, everyday life and migration, as well as economic trade and social structures. Her work often addresses themes such as identity, the human-nature relationship, and the social environment.
